name: webpack
one_liner: Static module bundler building optimised bundles from a dependency graph.
what_it_is: At its core a static module bundler for modern JavaScript applications, in its own words: from an entry point it builds an internal dependency graph and emits optimised bundles. Loaders and plugins let CSS, images and arbitrary assets be treated as modules in that graph.
why_it_matters: webpack is declining as a default, not as a technology — a distinction worth holding onto. It remains the most configurable bundler available and still builds a very large amount of production code. What changed is that cold-start and rebuild time became the dominant daily cost of front-end work, and native-speed alternatives closed most of the capability gap. Knowing webpack is still valuable, because you will inherit it. Choosing it for a new project now needs a specific reason you can name.
suitable_for: Existing projects with substantial webpack configuration already working
Builds with unusual asset pipelines that need its loader ecosystem
Module federation across separately deployed applications
not_suitable_for: Greenfield projects where dev-server startup and rebuild time matter
Teams with nobody willing to own build configuration long term
Simple static sites, where it is far more machinery than the job needs
